vulnerability_mechanism.summary: The golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent package does not validate the size of messages when processing identity requests containing certificates with constraints. A malformed message with an oversized constraint field causes a slice out-of-bounds read, resulting in a panic (denial of service). The security effect is a server crash in the Rancher process when serving SSH agent protocol requests during git operations with SSH credentials. The effect occurs because parseConstraints (a symbol listed in advisory adv-01) reads beyond the bounds of an internal buffer without size validation.

root_cause.summary: The vulnerability resides in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent package, specifically within parseConstraints which is one of the affected symbols listed in advisory adv-01 (id=adv-01, module=golang.org/x/crypto, package=golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent, symbols=[ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseConstraints]). The vulnerable package is used by Rancher through the ServeAgent function called in pkg/catalogv2/git/git.go:136: 'if err := agent.ServeAgent(*g.agent, conn); err != nil'. ServeAgent is the entry point that dispatches incoming SSH agent protocol messages to internal handlers, which in turn invoke parseConstraints when processing certificate constraint data in identity request messages. The root cause is the absence of bounds-checking in parseConstraints when parsing incoming protocol messages.

product_exposure.summary: The vulnerable functionality is exposed when Rancher performs git operations (clone, update) against Git-based Helm repositories configured with SSH credential authentication. When a secret of type corev1.SecretTypeSSHAuth is provided (git.go:83), the code adds the SSH private key to an in-memory agent keyring (git.go:88-96) and creates a Unix socket to serve agent requests during git commands (git.go:102-143). This is triggered from the gitCmd function (git.go:325) which calls injectAgent (git.go:337) when g.agent is set. Product scope: Rancher's catalogv2 git module for Git-based Helm repository operations. Build scope: go.mod declares golang.org/x/crypto v0.43.0 (go.mod:149), confirmed in go.sum hash at line 880. Platform: Linux (based on Unix socket usage at git.go:113-116). Deployment: Requires Rancher to have Git-based Helm repositories configured with SSH authentication secrets. Unknowns: exact deployment configuration (whether any Rancher instance actually uses SSH-authenticated git repos), network exposure of the Unix socket (local to git subprocess only), version of golang.org/x/crypto used at runtime.

alternative_paths.summary: Alternative manifestation checked: The pkg/api/steve/machine/ssh.go file imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh but not ssh/agent, so the ssh package client-side SSH usage (shell/dial operations) is not directly affected by this CVE. Transitive dependency check: no other go.mod in the workspace (hack/airgap, gotools, pkg/client, pkg/apis) declares a different version of golang.org/x/crypto that would override the main module's v0.43.0. The hack/airgap/go.mod has v0.25.0 but is a separate module not used by the main Rancher binary. ForwardToAgent is not directly called in this snapshot, but ServeAgent (which handles the same protocol processing) is actively used. Counterargument: the Unix socket created by injectAgent is scoped to a single git subprocess invocation and cleaned up afterward (git.go:126-127), limiting the attack surface to local code paths. However, the git process itself could be tricked by a malicious git remote or a compromised SSH key credential into connecting to an attacker-controlled agent, or an attacker with API access could trigger the code path to observe behavior. This limits but does not eliminate the attack surface.

This is triggered from the gitCmd function (git.go:325) which calls injectAgent (git.go:337) when g.agent is set. Product scope: Rancher's catalogv2 git module for Git-based Helm repository operations. Build scope: go.mod declares golang.org/x/crypto v0.43.0 (go.mod:149), confirmed in go.sum hash at line 880. Platform: Linux (based on Unix socket usage at git.go:113-116). Deployment: Requires Rancher to have Git-based Helm repositories configured with SSH authentication secrets. Unknowns: exact deployment configuration (whether any Rancher instance actually uses SSH-authenticated git repos), network exposure of the Unix socket (local to git subprocess only), version of golang.org/x/crypto used at runtime.

agent_assertions.statement: Alternative manifestation checked: The pkg/api/steve/machine/ssh.go file imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh but not ssh/agent, so the ssh package client-side SSH usage (shell/dial operations) is not directly affected by this CVE. Transitive dependency check: no other go.mod in the workspace (hack/airgap, gotools, pkg/client, pkg/apis) declares a different version of golang.org/x/crypto that would override the main module's v0.43.0. The hack/airgap/go.mod has v0.25.0 but is a separate module not used by the main Rancher binary. ForwardToAgent is not directly called in this snapshot, but ServeAgent (which handles the same protocol processing) is actively used. Counterargument: the Unix socket created by injectAgent is scoped to a single git subprocess invocation and cleaned up afterward (git.go:126-127), limiting the attack surface to local code paths. However, the git process itself could be tricked by a malicious git remote or a compromised SSH key credential into connecting to an attacker-controlled agent, or an attacker with API access could trigger the code path to observe behavior. This limits but does not eliminate the attack surface.

agent_output.reasoning: CVE-2025-47914 (GO-2025-4135) affects golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent, specifically the parseConstraints function which lacks message-size validation when processing SSH agent identity requests, potentially causing a panic due to out-of-bounds read. The snapshot declares golang.org/x/crypto v0.43.0 in go.mod (line 149), which falls in the affected range (introduced, fixed in 0.45.0, per advisory adv-01). The ssh/agent package is imported in pkg/catalogv2/git/git.go:24 and ServeAgent (listed in advisory symbols) is actively called at git.go:136 within the injectAgent function. This function creates a Unix domain socket to serve the SSH agent protocol for git SSH authentication operations. The attack surface is reachable: a Rancher user with API access to trigger git operations (Clone, Update) that use SSH credential authentication will have the vulnerable ServeAgent invoked. The agent processes incoming SSH agent protocol messages from git, and a malicious client connected to the Unix socket could send a malformed constraint message to trigger the out-of-bounds read and panic. No protection mechanism (configuration flag, runtime isolation, perimeter control) is evident in the snapshot that would block this attack surface. The component version (0.43.0) is confirmed below the fixed version (0.45.0) via go.mod line 149 and go.sum line 880.
